According to the listing, the stolen data includes detailed passenger profiles and operational records:  *   **Loyalty Program Data:** Full member accounts containing national IDs, passport numbers, home addresses, phone numbers, and tier status details. *   **Amadeus Booking Records:** Upcoming flight itineraries, traveler documents (passports/IDs), seat assignments, and ticket pricing. *   **Ground Transportation:** Limousine and home check-in bookings including vehicle details, driver information, and specific residential addresses (street, block, house numbers). *   **Live Driver Tracking:** Real-time GPS coordinates for drivers and passengers, along with ride status flags and contact details. *   **Financial & Operational Records:** Ancillary service payment ledgers, cargo manifests, aviation safety occurrence reports, and procurement documents.  The actor provides sample files hosted on file-sharing services to verify the authenticity of the leak and offers the full dataset for a negotiated price via Telegram. Kuwait Airways is the national flag carrier of Kuwait, serving as a critical hub in the Middle East with a substantial international passenger base. The exposure of national IDs and home addresses poses a severe risk of identity theft and physical security threats to passengers, while the live tracking data could facilitate targeted harassment or kidnapping risks during transit. 🇨🇦 CANADA: BELL CONFIRMS THEFT OF ENTERPRISE CUSTOMER DATA  Bell Canada says an intruder accessed some of its systems on November 17 and stole data belonging to some of its business customers. Bell says customer services were not disrupted.  What Bell has confirmed so far: • Entry point: a pre-production environment of Maximo, the system Bell uses to order and provision business circuits • Data taken: business contact details (names, job titles, work emails, phone numbers, business addresses), service ticket content and some IP addresses • Bell says no passwords or sensitive documents were affected • Intrusion contained and systems secured, according to Bell • Threat information shared with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security; RCMP cybercrime unit notified • Bell has not said how many customers are affected  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Bell described the attacker as using "agentic" capabilities but has not explained what that meant in this incident, and it does not establish that AI carried out the attack on its own. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions  ⚠️ Analyst Note: CVE-2026-123890 is the vCenter zero-day we reported on Nov 19. CVE-2026-129448 is the Apache Roller exploitation issue we reported on Nov 18. Federal agencies must act on all four by Nov 23. Known ransomware use: Unknown for all four. What the company has disclosed so far: • Suspicious activity detected; online order-taking suspended as a precaution • Outside cybersecurity experts engaged; investigation ongoing • Does not believe customer financial data was affected, because The Container Store does not retain consumer payment information • Incident isolated to The Container Store; Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY and Kirkland's were unaffected  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The disclosure does not confirm ransomware or say whether other customer data was taken. What the company has confirmed so far (as of 3 PM JST, Nov 20): • 4 client companies affected • About 49,000 records in total; this is a cumulative count and may include duplicates • Leaked data includes email addresses and other fields, which differ by client • No credit card data or My Number (national ID) numbers found in the leaked data so far • Affected clients were contacted individually and will notify their own customers • Services remain online; the incident has been reported to the relevant authorities  The intrusion route and full scope are still under investigation, and the numbers may change. The company has not named the affected clients or the specific service involved.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is the latest in a run of Japanese breaches at marketing and messaging vendors this month. Leaked email lists are often reused for phishing that copies a real brand. If you get an unexpected message tied to a Japanese online service, check it on the official site instead of clicking links. 🇬🇧 🚨 AURORA GANG CLAIMS WILLIAM COOK GROUP DATA BREACH  The Aurora ransomware group has added William Cook Holdings Limited (William Cook Group) to its leak site. The privately owned UK industrial group was founded in 1840 and is based in Sheffield. Its divisions include Cook Defence Systems, which makes track systems for armoured vehicles and is majority-owned by HEICO Corp, as well as William Cook Rail, William Cook Cast Products (steel castings for the nuclear, energy and naval sectors) and William Cook Intermodal.  Aurora claims it stole 1.1 TB, about 1.4 million files, from a file server at the Stanhope site. According to the group, the data includes: • Payroll databases with National Insurance numbers and bank details • Occupational health records, employment tribunal cases and liability claims • Financial records: accounting backups (2016–2022), management accounts (FY24–FY26) and bank transaction history through Aug 2026 • A commercial enquiry database • IT infrastructure data: an Active Directory permissions dump, endpoint security configuration and a VPN CA certificate • NDAs and cooperation agreements with defence partners, plus the chairman's personal files  The listing names BAE Systems, Babcock, General Dynamics, Rheinmetall and national ministries of defence among the group's customers. William Cook has not commented, and no reputable news report or official statement was found. The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If the claim is real, the supply-chain exposure matters more than the record count. A stolen AD permissions map, endpoint security config and VPN CA certificate could help attackers get back in or move toward partners. Defence primes buying from the group should check shared access and watch for phishing that uses procurement or NDA themes. Staff should watch for payroll and bank-detail fraud.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Ransomware #DataLeak #Aurora #WilliamCook #CookDefence #DefenceIndustry #SupplyChain #UK #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 CRYPTO: WAGYU'S WRAPPED MONERO TOKEN XMR1 CRASHES 99% AFTER ~$13.5M DUMP ON HYPERLIQUID  XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by swap service Wagyu, fell from about $490 to under $1 in roughly 30 minutes on Friday (Nov 20). A wallet funded by the token's creator address sold about $13.5 million worth on Hyperliquid.  What is reported so far: • The wallet received 5.2 million XMR1 in three transfers from the address that created the token • About 364,000 XMR1 were sold for roughly $13.5M, and part of the proceeds was swapped into ETH • About 4.8 million XMR1 reportedly remain in the same wallet • Wagyu's founder says he is still investigating, that market makers took most of the losses and that regular swaps were not affected • Monero (XMR) itself and Hyperliquid's XMR futures market were not affected  It is not yet confirmed whether the transfers were authorized or how they happened. No link has been shown to the data leak Wagyu disclosed on Oct 28.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: A wrapped asset is only as safe as the keys that can mint or move it. One account holding most of the supply is a single point of failure. XMR1 holders should expect fake "refund" and "claim" links. Only trust announcements from Wagyu's official channels.  Source (CoinDesk, Nov 20): coindesk.com/markets/2026/11… #DDW #Crypto #Wagyu #Monero #Hyperliquid #DeFi #CryptoHack
